finding.claim: Authorization result is discarded in dropTable, so any user passes. The same handler also concatenates the unvalidated form value `t` into a DROP TABLE statement, which is SQL injection. Sibling handler vacuum checks the error and returns 403.
finding.source: HTTP POST/GET to /admin/drop with form parameter t, from any actor that reaches the handler (userFrom needs a user in the request context, which no middleware in this file sets)

trace.note: route /admin/drop registered with no auth middleware
Authorize(u, "dba") return value ignored; execution continues when it returns an error
user-controlled t concatenated into DROP TABLE and executed

finding.guards_checked: Authorize error is not checked (api.go:26), unlike vacuum at api.go:33-36. No validation or allowlist on t. No auth middleware on the route (api.go:44). runSQL is a stub at api.go:41, so the real implementation was not available to inspect.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u,"dba") at api.go:26 is a bare statement whose error is discarded, so it blocks nothing. No allowlist or parameterization on t at api.go:27. No auth middleware on the route at api.go:44. The only incidental barrier is the unchecked type assertion in userFrom (api.go:22), which panics when no user is in the context. net/http recovers that panic and aborts the request.
verdict.reason: api.go:26 discards Authorize's error, and api.go:27 concatenates r.FormValue("t") into DROP TABLE, so any non-dba user whose request carries a user context (set elsewhere, since this file has no middleware at api.go:44) can drop arbitrary tables, unlike vacuum, which returns 403 at api.go:33-36. The "any actor" part of the source is overstated: an anonymous request with no user in context panics at api.go:22 before the sink, though that is a crash rather than a guard.
